items.followUp: What is an enzyme, and what substance does it act upon?

rubric.why: Identifies substrates as substances or reactants acted upon by enzymes.
rubric.description: Substrates are the substances or reactants on which enzymes act.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining substrates as substances or reactants acted upon by enzymes.

rubric.why: Explains how a substrate interacts with an enzyme or what happens to it.
rubric.description: A substrate binds to an enzyme's active site and is converted into product(s).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a substrate binds at an enzyme's active site or is converted into products.

modelAnswer: Substrates are the substances or reactants on which enzymes act.
A substrate binds to an enzyme's active site and is converted into product(s).

items.followUp: What is a coenzyme, and how does it help an enzyme?

rubric.why: Identifies a cofactor as a non protein component associated with an enzyme.
rubric.description: A cofactor is a non protein component associated with an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a cofactor as a non protein component associated with an enzyme.

rubric.why: States that cofactors are needed for enzyme activity or gives a valid type.
rubric.description: A cofactor is required for enzyme activity and may be an inorganic ion or an organic molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a cofactor is required for enzyme activity or naming a valid type.

modelAnswer: A cofactor is a non protein component associated with an enzyme.
It is required for the enzyme's activity and may be an inorganic ion or an organic molecule.

items.followUp: Describe the cellular and organ levels of organization in a living organism.

rubric.why: Describes how molecules are formed at the molecular level.
rubric.description: Atoms combine to form molecules at the molecular level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms combine to form molecules.

rubric.why: Links molecules with larger cell structures.
rubric.description: Molecules form or contribute to cell structures such as organelles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking molecules to organelles or other cell structures.

rubric.why: Defines a tissue as a group of similar cells.
rubric.description: A group of similar cells forms a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a tissue as a group of similar cells.

rubric.why: Explains that the cells in a tissue work together in a shared role.
rubric.description: The cells in a tissue work together to perform a particular function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that tissue cells perform a common or particular function.

modelAnswer: At the molecular level, atoms combine through chemical bonds to form molecules such as water, proteins and DNA.
Molecules form or contribute to cell structures, including organelles.
At the tissue level, a group of similar cells forms a tissue.
The cells in a tissue work together to perform a particular function.

items.followUp: Give two reasons why viruses are considered non living and two reasons why they show characteristics of living things.

rubric.why: States that viruses lack cellular organization.
rubric.description: Viruses are acellular and have no cellular structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses lack cellular structure.

rubric.why: Gives a feature showing the non living status of viruses outside a host.
rubric.description: Outside a host cell, viruses are inactive and cannot reproduce; they can even be crystallized.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid non living feature, such as inactivity outside a host or the ability to be crystallized.

rubric.why: States that viruses reproduce inside living host cells.
rubric.description: Inside a living host cell, viruses reproduce and show some characteristics of living things.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses reproduce inside a living host cell.

accept: boundary between living and non living
rubric.why: Gives the conclusion about the status of viruses.
rubric.description: Viruses are regarded as lying at the boundary between living and non living things.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses lie at the boundary between living and non living things.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular and have no cellular structure or independent metabolism.
Outside a host cell, they are inactive and cannot reproduce; they can even be crystallized.
Inside a living host cell, viruses reproduce and show some characteristics of living things.
Therefore, viruses are regarded as lying at the boundary between living and non living things.
